findings.description: The reports_archive bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects are stored with only S3 default encryption (or none, depending on configuration) rather than an explicit KMS/SSE-S3 policy. It also lacks the versioning present on peer buckets, so stored reports can be overwritten or deleted without recovery.

force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all of its contents to be deleted without emptying it first, removing the safety barrier that protects records from accidental or malicious destruction via a single Destroy/apply operation.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so account-level or bucket ACL settings can result in public exposure. The bucket also has no ACL set, leaving access control to defaults rather than explicit private configuration.

The ledger_exports bucket, which holds financial ledger data, has no server_side_encryption_configuration block and no versioning, leaving exported ledger data unencrypted with a defined key and unprotected against overwrite.
force_destroy = true permits destruction of the ledger bucket and its contents without an explicit empty step, weakening protection of financial records.
The model_artifacts bucket stores ML model artifacts and has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so artifacts are not encrypted with an explicit customer-managed key.
force_destroy = true allows the artifact bucket and all versions to be deleted in a single apply, bypassing the protections normally afforded by versioning.

The ops_runbooks bucket contains operational runbooks and has no server_side_encryption_configuration block; runbooks frequently embed hostnames, endpoints and credentials, so unencrypted storage is a meaningful exposure.
force_destroy = true allows the runbook bucket to be destroyed together with its contents in a single operation.

The audit_trail bucket is configured with acl = "log-delivery-write", a legacy canned ACL that grants the S3 log delivery group write and read-ACP access to the audit bucket. On a bucket that is itself the destination for access logging, this widens write access to the audit records beyond the owning account and relies on ACLs rather than bucket policy.
force_destroy = true on the audit trail bucket permits deletion of security-relevant logs and all their versions in a single apply, undermining the integrity of the audit record.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached to the audit bucket. Because it uses a legacy canned ACL rather than an explicit bucket policy plus public access block, an ACL misconfiguration could expose audit logs.

The seed object is uploaded without kms_key_id or server_side_encryption settings, so it is stored under whatever default the bucket provides; combined with the reports_archive bucket having no explicit encryption configuration, the object may be written unencrypted. The object's key and source also indicate a vendor roster, a data set that should be encrypted at rest.
